guard: a turn OpenCode killed is published as a run error, and a turn a person stopped is not
why: CELLS NAMED BEFORE THE RUN, not chosen from the wreckage afterwards.
O1 is the state this connector shipped in: `session.error` closed the run exactly as a finish
does, so an upstream API error and a completed turn were byte-identical on the wire. It is the
mutation that reproduces the defect, and the cell it must redden is the one that reproduced it.
O2 is the OPPOSITE failure and it is here because it is the easy one to ship by accident. A
person pressing Stop reaches this handler through the same bus event as a provider outage; a
blanket "session.error means the run failed" passes every failure cell in the suite and still
publishes a user's own cancellation as an error. Without O2 the suite could not tell a mapping
O3 was OpenCode's error name as the RUN_ERROR code. It is gone: since #1431 a published
RUN_ERROR carries no code, because upstream values can echo private text onto the events channel.
NOT REGISTERED, and named rather than left as a hole: nothing mutates the ORDER of the flush and
the close. Reversing them is a real defect and the reset suite already grades it; here it would
be a second copy of someone else's cell, and a mutation whose kill belongs to another file reads
as coverage this suite does not have.

mutations.name: O1 a failed turn closes exactly as a finished one does, which is the state this connector shipped in
mutations.find: await turnEnded(sessionID, eventHolder?.closeRun(Date.now(), interrupted ? undefined : runErrorOf(event.properties.error)));
mutations.expectRed: fail:and that close is RUN_ERROR, not RUN_FINISHED
mutations.cell: fail:and that close is RUN_ERROR, not RUN_FINISHED — THE DEFECT
mutations.note: The pre-fix line, restored verbatim. An APIError turn is published as a run that ended, carrying no outcome, and a reader cannot tell it from a turn that succeeded.

mutations.name: O2 every session.error becomes a failure, so a person's own Stop is published as one
mutations.cell: abort:and THAT close is RUN_FINISHED — a Stop is not a failed turn, and a blanket mapping would fail here
mutations.note: The plausible over-reach rather than a contrived one: the guard reads like a special case until you notice a user cancellation arrives on the same event.

mutations.name: O3 the error arm returns before the terminal's position read answers
mutations.find: await turnEnded(sessionID, eventHolder?.closeRun(Date.now(), interrupted ? undefined : runErrorOf(event.properties.error)));
mutations.replace: void turnEnded(sessionID, eventHolder?.closeRun(Date.now(), interrupted ? undefined : runErrorOf(event.properties.error)));
mutations.expectRed: barrier:the error arm is still in flight while the terminal's position read is held
mutations.note: The round-14 defect: the next turn was admitted before the position read answered, and the terminal named the next turn.

mutations.name: O4 the idle arm returns before the terminal's position read answers
mutations.expectRed: barrier:the idle arm is still in flight while the terminal's position read is held

mutations.name: O5 a native prompt passes the turn end still settling
mutations.expectRed: barrier:a native prompt is held while the terminal's position read is held
mutations.note: The round-15 defect: the driven path waited for the close's position read and the prompt typed into the TUI did not, so a failed turn closed as a finish and its successor as the error.

mutations.name: O6 a record at or before the reported turn end is settled only by its own marks
mutations.expectRed: unsettled:the turn after it is published, so the session is not wedged behind the unfinished part
mutations.note: The round-16 defect: a part still filling when its turn died never gets its end mark and its message never reports completed, so every later read stopped at it and no later turn was published.

mutations.name: O7 the session's barrier is the latest turn end alone, not every one still settling
mutations.expectRed: twice:a native prompt is still held while the EARLIER turn end's read is held
mutations.note: The round-18 defect: a turn that ended twice, by its error and the idle after it, had its barrier replaced by the later turn end, whose read answered first and deleted it while the error's read was still pending.
